How Much Does a Yard of Topsoil Weigh?

A cubic yard of topsoil weighs about 2,200 lbs (1.1 tons) when dry. Moisture content and soil composition can push the weight up or down significantly.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a cubic yard of topsoil weigh?

A cubic yard of dry topsoil weighs approximately 2,200 lbs (1.1 tons). Wet or heavy clay topsoil can weigh significantly more — up to 3,000 lbs per cubic yard in some cases.

How many 40-lb bags of topsoil equal a cubic yard?

It takes 36 bags of 40 lb topsoil to equal one cubic yard, since each bag contains about 0.75 cubic feet (27 ÷ 0.75 = 36).

Can I haul topsoil in a pickup truck?

A standard half-ton pickup can safely carry about 1,000 lbs — less than half a cubic yard of topsoil. A 3/4-ton or 1-ton truck can carry a full cubic yard. Always stay within your truck's payload rating.

How many cubic yards of topsoil are in a ton?

One ton of topsoil equals about 0.91 cubic yards (1 ÷ 1.10 t/cu yd). Two tons equals about 1.82 cubic yards.
